note: Destination buffer for decoded TGA pixels is allocated with malloc (no zeroing). For the RLE branch no memset is ever applied to it, so every byte not covered by a successful read stays uninitialized.
RLE decode cursor is set to point into the uninitialized heap buffer.
Packet repeat count decoded from the file-supplied packet header byte; for the crafted byte 0x80, count == 1, so count * pixel_size equals the remaining image size.
num becomes exactly 0, so the while (num > 0) loop exits without a further atEnd() re-check and without the num < 0 guard (line 242) firing; 'valid' remains true.

Return value is ignored: at EOF on the truncated file this reads 0 bytes and leaves the stack buffer pixel[] uninitialized. Unlike the non-RLE branch (lines 270-272) there is no memset fallback for the destination, so the buffer keeps uninitialized bytes.
The uninitialized pixel byte is copied into the image buffer, propagating uninitialized (poisoned) data from the stack into the heap destination.
Palette conversion reads the uninitialized byte from the image buffer into idx.

code: scanline[x] = qRgb(palette[3 * idx + 2], palette[3 * idx + 1], palette[3 * idx + 0]);
note: The uninitialized idx is used as an array index into the palette: use of uninitialized memory (MemorySanitizer report point).
